effect: Conquering a whole country now passes its state debt to the conquerors with its assets, as state succession does in practice (Vienna Convention 1983: state debt passes with the territory, in equitable shares when there are several successors), instead of writing the debt off. When a country is wiped out, the game hands its treasury cash, FX reserves and sovereign fund to the conquerors in proportion to the population each takes (VXg), then its retirement writes every bond down to zero (oxB, sovereign_retirement_write_down): the bondholders (its own banks, now the conqueror's, its households, foreigners, central banks) took the whole loss and the conqueror kept the assets debt-free. Now, right after the assets are handed over and before the write-down step: (1) each conqueror other than the heir issues the conquered treasury a succession bond for its population share of the debt being inherited (the conquered state's bond face, net of the succession claims it holds and of the claims held wholly by the heir's treasury, its succession claims and bilateral loans to the conquered state, which the takeover releases (xsg) rather than passes on), with the game's secession bond (QxB, sovereign_debt_succession: in that conqueror's currency, at the conquered state's average rate and maturity); shares under a millionth of a billion are not booked. (2) Treasury obligations between the conquered state and the heir (e.g. unpaid electricity bills between them) are cancelled the way the game's retirement cancels them (economic_obligation_country_retirement). Since build 26368058 the game retires all of a dead state's open obligations among its early retirement steps, before this succession; for a conquest W3 takes over, that step now keeps the conquered treasury's obligations with other living countries (its unpaid bills to and from them) open, and the obligation move in (3) passes them to the heir as before. If W3 refuses the takeover, they are retired right after, as the unmodified game does. Obligations between the conquered treasury and the heir's are retired in that early step as in the unmodified game, so step (2) finds none on this build; it stays for the case where the early step leaves one. (3) The conqueror that takes the most population (the game's own heir for the retirement, tkQ, the one that also seizes the nuclear arsenal) takes over the conquered treasury through the finance part of the game's own integration succession (TdQ: strategic stocks $CQ, accounts and bonds exB, obligations OnB, project funding taB). Every bond keeps its holders, amounts, coupon, maturity and currency and is now issued by the heir; the other treasury balances pass too (budget and military cash, payables and receivables, funding need, strategic stocks). (4) Succession claims the conquered treasury holds on other countries, including the bonds from step 1, pass to the heir with the heir as creditor: the game's integration succession moves only bilateral positions and would leave these with the dead treasury, where the debtor's settlement (oiA) writes them off as dead-creditor claims. Claims between the heir and the conquered state then cancel (xsg), as in integration. (5) Inherited bonds are reclassified as domestic or foreign-currency debt against the heir's currency, as the game's currency reform does (a euro bond inherited by Switzerland becomes foreign-currency debt). No debt, bond or money is created or lost: the write-off step then finds no debt. If either treasury is in a state the game's succession code would reject (missing or closed account, inconsistent strategic stock), nothing is moved and the game's write-off applies as before (a console warning names the reason). The other conquerors' bonds (step 1) are not prechecked: a fault there would leave the first bonds booked without the succession; it needs a conqueror without working treasury accounts, which the game's own save check already rejects. Since build 26346311 the game itself moves the conquered strategic reserves to the heir (F9A) right after this succession; when W3 has taken over the treasury it has already moved them, so that second move is skipped (it would find the reserve accounts already the heir's and fault with strategic-reserve:account); when W3 refuses, the game's move runs as in the unmodified game. The obligation move is the game's rewritten NsB (since 26346311), which also extinguishes obligations whose payer and payee end up the same treasury. Since build 26368058 the game's project-funding move (now IuB) also hands the conquered country's military-industry projects to the heir, as it does in peaceful integration; without W3 they disappear with the dead country, as in the unmodified game. Not changed: IMF credit to the conquered state is still written off (LEQ); peaceful integration already moved the debt; partial annexation moves no debt (W4). The heir's debt ratio rises by the debt taken over, which its rating sees. Saved state: only the game's own instruments, positions, accounts and sovereign records. Day 0 unchanged (no conquest at start). Minified names are those of build 26318758, except those named with build 26346311 or 26368058.
